title: AI for Coding and Technical Tasks
description: How to use AI for coding — from writing your first script to reviewing complex code — even if you have never programmed before.

data.text: AI has transformed coding more than almost any other knowledge domain. Developers ship features faster. And non-developers — for the first time — can create working scripts, formulas, and automation snippets without years of programming experience. This lesson covers both cases and adds practical patterns for testing, security, and integrating AI into developer workflows.
Four ways AI assists with code

data.title: Write new code — complete prompt template
data.content:
"Write a [language] [function / script / class] that:
- Takes [input description] as input
- Does [behavior, step by step]
- Returns [output description]
- Handles the edge case where [edge case]

Add comments explaining each major step. Use [specific library if known]."

data.title: Debug a problem
data.content:
"This [language] code is supposed to [describe goal] but instead it [describe behavior or error message].

Code:
[paste code]

Error message:
[paste error]

What is wrong, and how do I fix it? Explain why the error occurs."

data.title: Ask for improvements
data.content:
"Review this code for: (1) bugs or edge cases it does not handle, (2) performance issues if it runs on large data, (3) readability — could it be easier to understand? Show specific suggestions with the improved code.

[paste code]"

data.text: Prompt patterns that work well for coding

items: Role + goal: "You are an experienced Python engineer. Write..."
Input → Output examples: provide 1–2 examples of input and expected output for deterministic tasks
Constraints-first: list constraints (libraries, runtime, memory) before the task
Test-driven prompt: ask the model to produce unit tests alongside implementation
Explain-then-code: request a short plan or pseudocode before the final implementation

data.caption: A simple pair-programming loop: propose → implement → test → review → iterate
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  User["Developer / Non-coder"] --> Propose["Ask AI: propose approach / pseudocode"]
  Propose --> Implement["AI: generate code"]
  Implement --> Test["Run tests / sample inputs"]
  Test --> Review["AI or human reviews failures"]
  Review --> Iterate["Refine code or tests"]
  Iterate --> Implement

  style Propose fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style Implement fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style Test fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37
  style Review fill:#eddff8,stroke:#8250df

data.text: Use the AI as a collaborator: ask for a short plan, request code, run quick tests, and then ask the AI to explain failing tests. This loop keeps you in control and reduces the chance of subtle bugs slipping into production.
Testing, reproducibility, and CI for AI-generated code

Treat AI-generated code like any other contribution: add unit tests, integration tests, and include the code snippet and prompt in your repository. For production use, include the prompt and model settings in your CI pipeline so changes to prompts or model versions trigger test runs.

data.caption: CI pipeline for AI-generated code: prompt + code → tests → benchmark → deploy
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  Prompt["Prompt + model settings"] --> Gen["Generate code"]
  Gen --> Tests["Run unit & integration tests"]
  Tests --> Bench["Record performance & correctness"]
  Bench --> Gate["Pass? (manual gate for prod) "]
  Gate -->|Yes| Deploy["Deploy to staging / prod"]
  Gate -->|No| Notify["Notify owner for review"]

  style Prompt fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style Gen fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style Tests fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37
  style Bench fill:#ffe1cc,stroke:#bc4c00

rows: Code passes simple tests but fails edge cases
Write unit tests covering edge cases; use property-based tests
Run static analysis, dependency checks, and security review
AI assumes data formats or APIs behave differently
Include explicit input schemas and sample payloads in prompt
Fix model settings (temperature), save prompt and seed, prefer deterministic sampling

data.title: Never paste sensitive credentials into AI
data.text: Never paste API keys, passwords, database connection strings, or authentication tokens into any AI chatbot. Remove them before pasting and replace with placeholders like YOUR_API_KEY. AI-generated code can also introduce security vulnerabilities — always review code that handles user input, file access, or authentication.

Always test AI-generated code before using it in production. It can look correct and still have subtle bugs on edge cases. For anything handling money, authentication, or user data — have a developer review it.
How to integrate AI into your development workflow

items: Editor augmentation: use Copilot or Cursor for inline suggestions and completions while coding.
Code review assistant: ask the model to produce a review checklist and suggested fixes for a PR.
Automated test generation: request unit tests for new functions and include them in CI.
Documentation generation: generate README sections, usage examples, and API docs from code and docstrings.

data.title: Generate a CSV filter script
data.content: "Write a Python script that reads input.csv, filters rows where 'status' == 'active' and 'signup_date' is within the last 90 days, and writes filtered.csv. Include a --dry-run flag that prints the number of rows without writing the file. Use pandas and include comments."

data.title: Create unit tests alongside implementation
data.content: "Implement function `calculate_commission(sales, rate)` and also provide pytest unit tests covering: normal case, zero sales, negative rate (raise ValueError), and very large numbers. Return both implementation and tests in separate code blocks."

items: Always include sample inputs and expected outputs in prompts for deterministic tasks.
Ask the model to produce tests and run them locally before trusting results.
Keep prompts and model settings versioned alongside code.
Prefer deterministic model settings for production code generation (low temperature).
Use static analysis and dependency scanning on AI-generated code.

data.title: AI for coding essentials
points: Non-coders: AI can write Excel formulas, Python scripts, SQL queries, regex, and HTML — just describe what you need
The four modes: write, explain, debug, and review — all in natural language
For in-editor use: GitHub Copilot (free) or Cursor (more powerful)
For one-off tasks: ChatGPT or Claude in the browser
Never paste credentials into AI — use placeholders
Test, review, and version AI-generated code before using it in production
